title: Painting FAQ: Cost, Timeline, Prep & Warranty
description: Straight answers on house painting cost factors, timelines, prep, products, coats, warranty, and scheduling from a North Central Florida painting contractor.
heroIntro: Homeowners and property managers across North Central Florida ask us the same handful of questions before they hire a painter. Here are our answers.

sections.h2: Why two painting quotes can be so far apart
body: This is the question behind most house painting questions in North Central Florida: why do two bids for the same house differ so much? Usually it's because they cover different work. One bid includes washing, scraping to a sound edge, replacing a soft fascia board, re-caulking every moving joint, and two full coats of a premium acrylic. The other bid is one coat over whatever's already there. Both say "paint the exterior," but only one of them will hold up.

We price from five things: measured area, surface condition and prep, product line, access and height, and the number of colors. Color itself hardly changes the price. Condition changes it a lot. Chalky siding, mildew on a shaded wall, or rot at a window sill all add labor, and a quote that leaves them out is cheaper because it does less.

A single interior room is usually done in one day. A whole-home interior runs three days to two weeks. A full exterior takes three to seven working days, plus time to wash and let the surfaces dry. Most projects start one to three weeks after you approve the estimate.

Season matters more outside than inside. October through May is the best stretch for exterior house painting. During summer we start earlier in the day and watch dew point and radar closely. Our article on how Florida weather affects painting covers this in more detail. Interiors can be painted any month.

sections.h2: Questions about products, coats, and prep
body: Two full coats is our minimum. We add a third for dramatic color changes or porous surfaces. The product depends on what we're painting: 100% acrylic on siding and trim, elastomeric on stucco that moves, waterborne urethane enamel on cabinets and doors, and penetrating stain on bare wood. If you're torn on sheen, our guide to choosing a paint finish for each room lays out the tradeoffs.
Repairs are part of prep, not an extra. That includes nail pops, drywall patches, rotted trim, and failed caulk. Each item is listed on the estimate so nothing gets painted over and forgotten.

sections.h2: Questions about living with the project
body: Most homeowners stay home during an interior repaint. The crew moves and covers furniture, masks floors, and works one room at a time, so the rest of the house stays usable. If odor is a concern, for example with a nursery, a home office, or someone sensitive to smells, we can use low-VOC options. Commercial projects can run on nights and weekends so staff and customers aren't affected.

For exterior work, we'll ask you to move cars away from the walls and keep pets inside on spray days. Expect a wash day before painting starts, then a pause while everything dries. That gap is part of the plan. Painting damp siding in humid weather leads to early peeling.

sections.h2: Get everything in writing, whoever you hire
body: Our advice applies to any painter you're considering, us included. Ask for surfaces included and excluded, prep steps, product line, number of coats, and warranty terms in writing. A one-page scope like that prevents most disputes before they happen. Our free written estimates include all of it. If you still have a question after reading this page, get in touch and a crew lead will answer it.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to paint a house in North Central Florida?
faqs.a: We don't publish prices because the biggest variable is surface condition. Measured area, prep and repair, product line, access and height, and the number of colors set the price. A free walkthrough gets you an itemized written number.

faqs.q: Do I need to move furniture or leave the house?
faqs.a: No. Our crews move and protect furniture and work room by room, so you can stay home during an interior repaint.

faqs.q: Can you match an existing color?
faqs.a: Yes. We can match from a paint chip, a cabinet door, or a leftover can, and we make full-size drawdowns so you can approve the match before we paint.

Yes. Exterior projects carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. We also leave labeled touch-up paint and fix anything at the final walkthrough before closing out the job.
We serve 15 cities across Alachua, Marion, Levy, Columbia, and Gilchrist counties. Gainesville and Ocala are our two largest markets.
